keyframes.caption: On the night of 1 May 2011, a secret American force prepared to fly from Jalalabad into Pakistan.
Two modified Black Hawk helicopters lifted off with about two dozen special operators, an interpreter, and a dog named Cairo.
Far behind them, backup Chinooks waited in case the assault force needed help or another aircraft.
Over Abbottabad, a surveillance drone circled in darkness and relayed the approaching helicopters to commanders.
After about 90 minutes in the air, the helicopters reached the compound without warning the city below.
As Modified Black Hawk 1 settled over the high walls, it lost lift and came down hard inside the yard.
At the guest house, courier Abu Ahmed al-Kuwaiti opened fire. The assault team returned fire and killed him.
The teams pressed through the inner gate while a second group sealed the streets outside the compound.
Inside the main house, Abrar al-Kuwaiti and his wife Bushra were killed during the clearing of the ground floor.
Moving up the narrow stairs, the operators encountered and killed Khalid bin Laden.
On the third floor, the operators found and killed Osama bin Laden. The message Geronimo, E K I A, was sent back.
With the fighting over, the team gathered computers and documents while women and children were moved into the yard.
The damaged Modified Black Hawk could not fly out, so one of the waiting Chinooks was called forward.
Before leaving, the team destroyed the crippled helicopter to keep its secret technology from being recovered.

After about 38 minutes on the ground, the force left Abbottabad without suffering an American casualty.
The mission was over. Its name was Operation Neptune Spear.
By morning, the compound had become the focus of the world and satellites were recording the aftermath.

In daylight, the damaged compound and the remains of the helicopter could be seen from above.
The morning after the raid, satellite images preserved the first clear record of what had happened here.
